title: Art Department
tagline: I art-direct a designer, a 3D studio and a voice actor.
what: I direct the people who make our visuals, a contract designer and an outside 3D studio, and I make plenty of it myself.
does: Brief and review a contract designer, with one set of rules for every request
Direct a 3D render studio through models, renders and revision rounds
Script product videos, cast a voice actor and approve the final read
Shoot reference footage for the animators myself
Publish videos with thumbnails and descriptions
Keep the brand kit: logos, voice and style guide
Design hang tags, labels, decals, trophies, patches and shirt mockups myself
Lay out brochures, posters, banners and infographics, sized for local print

solved.problem: Product videos needed a consistent order, pace and voice.
solved.did: Wrote the order and speed down as a standard, reviewed round by round, then lined up scripts and a voice actor.
solved.ended: The finished videos came back with scripts and voice, and one was reused as an intro later.

solved.problem: Hundreds of product photos needed clean cutouts.
solved.did: Scoped the batch, sent the main photos to the designer first, and added a check that catches cutout flaws.
solved.ended: Approved photos now live in one library.

solved.problem: Design requests arrived in every shape, so the designer lost time decoding them.
solved.did: Wrote the briefing rules: where work gets queued, how priority is set, how a brief reads, and where files and share links live.
solved.ended: Briefs follow one set of rules now, and the busiest month held thirteen design projects.

worksWith: A contract designer, a 3D render studio, a voice actor, printers, leadership, customer service, a developer.
story: I built a repeatable way to get product models from a 3D studio reviewed and approved. The plan covered 14 products and 67 models, starting with a small pilot.
We wanted customers to see and spin a product before buying it, and needed models built from the real products.

I wrote the model spec, set the file names and built a tracking board. Upload checks compare scale, connection points and textures, followed by a fit check against the real part. The studio and I work from the same short standard.
The first model passed from start to finish. After that, approved models started arriving steadily, each through the same review.
credit: The job, plus the tools I built for it
